framework: FBISE Assessment Framework (National Curriculum of Pakistan 2022-23)
subject: Physics

source.publisher: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
source.licence: Government publication; structure + our own wording only

outcomes.text: Define gravitational field strength and calculate it for a point mass.
Read gravitational fields from field lines; treat a uniform sphere as a point mass.
Use Newton's law of gravitation to find the force between two point masses.
Derive g = GM/r squared from Newton's law and the field definition.
Explain why g stays almost constant for small height changes near Earth.
Link gravitational force to centripetal acceleration to study circular orbits.
Describe geostationary satellites: 24-hour period, over the equator, west to east.
Define gravitational potential and calculate it for a point mass.
Show how potential gives the potential energy of two masses and use it.
Explain how moving molecules create gas pressure.
Derive and use pV = (1/3)Nm<c squared>.
Calculate the root-mean-square speed of an ideal gas.
Derive and use the mean translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule.

subtopics.title: Ideal gas model and extreme matter

outcomes.text: Recognise the ideal-gas model as the base of statistical mechanics.
Know that extreme conditions create unusual states such as degenerate matter and Bose-Einstein condensates.
Give simple examples of free oscillations.
Use displacement, amplitude, period, frequency, angular frequency and phase difference.
Write the SHM period using frequency and angular frequency.
Explain that SHM has acceleration proportional to displacement and opposite to it.
Solve problems with a = -omega squared x.
Use the velocity equations of SHM to solve problems.
Read graphs of displacement, velocity and acceleration in SHM.
Describe how kinetic and potential energy swap during SHM.
Use the total-energy formula of SHM in problems.
Explain how a resistive force damps an oscillator.
Use the terms light, critical and heavy damping.
Sketch displacement-time graphs for each damping type.
Give practical examples of damped oscillations and why critical damping matters.
Justify critical damping in a car suspension.
State that resonance gives maximum amplitude at the natural frequency.
Give practical examples of free and forced oscillations.
Explain what sets the frequency response and sharpness of resonance.
Name uses of standing waves and resonance such as Rubens tubes and Chladni plates.
Judge when resonance helps and when it must be avoided.
Explain experiments showing two-source interference with water, sound, light and microwaves.
State the conditions for visible two-source interference fringes.
Solve double-slit problems with the fringe spacing formula.
Use d sin(theta) = n lambda to solve problems.
Describe how a diffraction grating measures the wavelength of light.
Outline the Copenhagen and many-worlds readings of electron double-slit results.
Define electric potential and calculate it for a point charge.
Use the field as the negative of the potential gradient.
Show how potential gives the energy of two point charges and use it.
Define and calculate capacitance for a sphere and parallel plates.
Derive and use the formulas for capacitors in series and parallel.
Solve problems with series and parallel capacitors.

subtopics.title: Energy and discharge of a capacitor

outcomes.text: Find the stored energy from the area under the V-Q graph.
Analyse graphs of p.d., charge and current in a discharging capacitor; use tau = RC.
Use the exponential discharge equations.
List capacitor uses in everyday devices.
Describe how animal cells make electrical signals using ion channels.
Know that some aquatic animals make electric shocks, like the electric eel.
Explain electroreception with animal examples.
Use period, frequency and peak value for alternating current and voltage.
Use sinusoidal equations for AC current or voltage.
Know that mean power in a resistor is half the peak power.
Tell r.m.s. from peak values and use the relation.
Tell half-wave from full-wave rectification on graphs.
Explain half-wave rectification with one diode.
Explain full-wave rectification with a four-diode bridge.
Show how a capacitor smooths rectified current.
Define mutual and self inductance and the henry.
Describe AC phase and how it leads or lags.
Identify inductors as chokes in AC circuits.
Calculate capacitor and inductor reactance.
Describe impedance as the vector sum of resistance and reactance.
State that radiation has a particle nature.
Use E = hf and the electronvolt in problems.
Explain photon momentum p = E/c.
Describe photoelectron emission from an illuminated metal.
Use threshold frequency and threshold wavelength.
Explain photoemission with photon energy and work function.
State and apply hf = work function + max kinetic energy.
Explain why the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on frequency, not intensity.
Compare evidence for light as a wave and as a particle.
Explain what electron diffraction shows about matter waves.
Use the de Broglie wavelength in problems.
State and explain Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.
Use the uncertainty principle to explain why experiments cannot be exact.
State that isolated atoms have discrete electron energy levels.
Explain how emission and absorption line spectra form.
Use hf = delta E to solve problems.
Describe the Compton effect qualitatively.
Explain pair production and pair annihilation.
Explain how electron microscopes get high resolution.
Recognise the equivalence of mass and energy.
Define and use mass defect and binding energy.
Sketch binding energy per nucleon against nucleon number.
Recall what fusion and fission mean.
Explain how binding energy per nucleon relates to fusion and fission, and how fission neutrons start a chain reaction.
Calculate the energy released in nuclear reactions.
Explain how count-rate fluctuations show decay is random.
Explain that decay is spontaneous and random.
Define activity and the decay constant and state how they connect.
Explain half-life with examples.
Use lambda = 0.693/T to solve numerical problems.
State that radioactive decay is exponential.
Use the exponential decay relation for activity, count rate or number of nuclei.
Describe the main parts of a nuclear reactor.
Explain why uranium fuel is enriched.
Compare the energy from fission with chemical reactions.
Explain what a medical tracer is.
Explain annihilation of particle and antiparticle.
Illustrate how PET scanning works.
Calculate the energy of gamma photons from annihilation.
Explain why annihilation gamma photons travel in opposite directions.
Explain luminosity as the total power radiated by a star.
Apply the inverse square law for radiant flux.
Define standard candles and how they give distances to galaxies.
Explain blackbody radiation and apply Wien's law to find a star's temperature.
Apply the Stefan-Boltzmann law to solve problems.
Estimate a star's radius from its luminosity and temperature.
Explain what the lines in emission and absorption spectra tell us.
Explain how redshift suggests the Universe is expanding.
State Hubble's law and how it leads to the Big Bang.
Describe Earth's climate as a complex system.
Relate ocean currents and winds to climate.
Explain climate inertia.
Explain that climate change has internal and external causes.
Explain how energy transfer sets global climate.
Explain how Earth's rotation turns air and forms atmospheric cells.
Explain why saltier ocean water is denser.
Explain how thermohaline circulation moves heat.
Explain how climate science shows chaotic behaviour.
Explain the piezo-electric effect and its use.
Explain how ultrasound gives diagnostic images.
Explain how X-rays form by electron bombardment.
Explain how X-rays image the inside of the body.
Explain how CT scanning works.
Explain with examples what simplicity and symmetry mean as mathematical beauty.
Give an example against the claim that physical truths must be elegant.
Weigh pros and cons in debates such as searching for aliens and pursuing risky research.
Explain how thought experiments such as Newton's cannonball convey physics ideas.
Develop safety guidelines for a proposed experiment.
Form a testable hypothesis by naming independent, dependent and controlled variables.
Explain how to vary and measure the variables.
Explain how the data will be analysed.
Suggest how technology can digitise data.
Show absolute uncertainty beside every measurement.
Show error bars in both directions.
Draw a best-fit line and a worst acceptable line.
Rearrange expressions into straight-line forms.
Use a y against x graph to find constants.
Use a log y against log x graph to find constants.
Use a ln y against x graph to find constants.
Decide which derived quantities to calculate from raw data.
Convert absolute uncertainty into fractional or percentage form.
Calculate uncertainty in derived quantities.
Estimate uncertainty in a graph's gradient.
Estimate uncertainty in a graph's y-intercept.
Write a result as a value, uncertainty and unit.
